## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design a controlled canary workflow in a single namespace, including secure tag retrieval, canary deployment, health window, promote/rollback logic, and per-namespace logging.

## Key Concepts

- CronJob orchestration
- Canary patterns without specialized controllers
- Readiness probes and health checks
- Secret-based API tokens
- InitContainers for tooling
- PVC-based logs
- Namespace NetworkPolicy

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: ns-canary-rollback
spec:
  schedule: "*/10 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
          - name: orchestrator
            image: myorg/canary-orchestrator:latest
            envFrom:
            - secretRef:
                name: api-token
            - configMapRef: ... # canary config
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you extend to multiple namespaces? 
- How would you tune health-check thresholds and rollback criteria?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests CKAD basics in a slightly different data path: file-based ingestion, ConfigMap-driven batching, and integrating InitContainers, Secrets, TLS sidecars, and networking policies in a realistic per-namespace pattern. It also probes how a candidate balances durability vs. simplicity in a beginner task.

## Key Concepts
- ConfigMapKeyRef for BATCH_SIZE
- PVC-based volumes and multi-moint approach
- InitContainer provisioning (python3, watchdog)
- Sidecar for TLS/certs
- Secrets for credentials
- Readiness/Liveness probes
- Namespace NetworkPolicy to restrict egress

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: log-collector-config
data:
  BATCH_SIZE: "100"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: log-portal-creds
type: Opaque
data:
  username: <base64>
  password: <base64>
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: log-collector
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: installer
        image: alpine:3.18
        command: ["sh","-c","apk add --no-cache python3 py3-pip && pip3 install watchdog"]
      containers:
      - name: watcher
        image: my-registry/log-watcher:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: /logs
          name: logs
        - mountPath: /summaries
          name: summaries
        env:
        - name: BATCH_SIZE
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: log-collector-config
              key: BATCH_SIZE
      volumes:
      - name: logs
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: logs-pvc
      - name: summaries
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: summaries-pvc
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you modify this to ensure at-least-once delivery of the digest? 
- What changes would you make to support multiple namespaces scaling this pattern effectively?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Explores practical CKAD competencies: deployment orchestration, config/secret management, volumes, autoscaling, service exposure, and network isolation.

## Key Concepts
- Deployment, PVC, ConfigMap/Secret, HPA
- ClusterIP service semantics
- NetworkPolicy gating and its limitations

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: my-app
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: my-app:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        envFrom:
        - configMapRef:
            name: my-app-config
        - secretRef:
            name: my-app-creds
        volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /data
      volumes:
      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: data-pvc
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: data-pvc
spec:
  accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
  storageClassName: standard
---
apiVersion: autoscaling/v1
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: my-app-hpa
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: my-app
  minReplicas: 3
  maxReplicas: 10
  targetCPUUtilizationPercentage: 60
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: my-app
spec:
  selector:
    app: my-app
  ports:
  - port: 8080
    targetPort: 8080
  type: ClusterIP
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-egress-api
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: my-app
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 203.0.113.0/24
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test this in a cluster with a restricted CNI?
- What changes if the app becomes stateful or requires dynamic PVC provisioning?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Explores per-namespace data ingestion, config-driven parsing, and strict egress controls—core CKAD topics with practical trade-offs.

## Key Concepts
- ConfigMaps for runtime parsing rules
- PVC-backed logs and InitContainers for tooling
- Secrets for credentials and tokens
- TLS sidecar and cert rotation
- Readiness/Liveness probes
- Namespace NetworkPolicy egress controls

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal skeleton: Deployment, PVC, ConfigMap/Secret refs
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: log-router
  namespace: <namespace>
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: log-router
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: log-router
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: install-tools
        image: alpine:3.18
        command: ["/bin/sh","-c","apk add --no-cache awk sed curl"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
      containers:
      - name: router
        image: myorg/log-router:latest
        env:
        - name: REGEX
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: log-config
              key: regex
        - name: BATCH_SIZE
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: log-config
              key: batchSize
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
      volumes:
      - name: logs
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: logs-pvc
      - name: tls
        secret:
          secretName: log-tls
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test the regex parsing and batching in a SRP-safe way?
- What metrics would you expose for reliability and observability?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question validates understanding of per-namespace resource governance in Kubernetes. It tests knowledge of how LimitRange and ResourceQuota work together to control pod sizing and cluster resource allocation.

## Key Concepts
- **LimitRange**: Sets default requests/limits applied to Pods that don't specify resources
- **ResourceQuota**: Enforces hard limits on total namespace resource consumption
- **Policy alignment**: Ensuring Deployments specify resources matching namespace defaults
- **Verification**: Testing policy enforcement with intentional over-allocation
- **Rollback**: Strategy for removing or scaling back resources when policies need adjustment

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: analytics-lr
  namespace: analytics
spec:
  limits:
  - type: Container
    default:
      cpu: "200m"
      memory: 256Mi
    defaultRequest:
      cpu: "100m"
      memory: 128Mi
```
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: analytics-quo
  namespace: analytics
spec:
  hard:
    cpu: "400m"
    memory: 512Mi
    requests.storage: "1Gi"
```
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: reporter
  namespace: analytics
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: reporter
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "100m"
            memory: "128Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "200m"
            memory: "256Mi"
```
## Verification Commands
```bash
kubectl apply -f limitrange.yaml
kubectl apply -f quota.yaml
kubectl apply -f deployment.yaml
kubectl describe resourcequota analytics-quo -n analytics
kubectl run overload-test --image=busybox --restart=Never --requests=cpu=500m,memory=600Mi --dry-run=server
```
## Rollback Strategy
```bash
kubectl delete -f quota.yaml
kubectl delete -f limitrange.yaml
kubectl scale deployment reporter --replicas=0 -n analytics
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to implement a practical, namespace-scoped canary upgrade using standard CKAD tools: CronJob scheduling, patching Deployments, ConfigMaps/Secrets for config and credentials, and PVC-based logging. It also exercises InitContainers, probes, and network policy considerations in a real workflow.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob scheduling and JobTemplate execution
- Patching Deployment images with kubectl set image or patch
- Reading image tag from ConfigMap and registry authentication via Secret
- Persisting status in a ConfigMap and logging to a PVC
- InitContainer to install tooling (kubectl, jq)
- Readiness/Liveness probes for the Job Pod
- Namespace NetworkPolicy restricting registry egress

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: canary-upgrade
spec:
  schedule: "*/10 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: canary-sa
          initContainers:
          - name: install-tools
            image: alpine:3.17
            command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache curl jq; true"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
          containers:
          - name: upgrader
            image: bitnami/kubectl:latest
            command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "set -e; CANARY_TAG=$(kubectl get configmap canary-config -o jsonpath='{.data.tag}'); kubectl patch deployment my-app -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"my-app","image":"myrepo/my-app:${CANARY_TAG}"}]}}}}' --record; echo done; sleep 1"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
          volumes:
          - name: logs
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: logs-pvc
          imagePullSecrets:
          - name: registry-credentials
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How to implement idempotent patches and roll back on failure?
- How to measure canary success (latency, error rate) before full rollout?
- How would this scale across many namespaces or deployments?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests practical lifecycle management and how probes interact with rolling updates to avoid downtime.

## Key Concepts

- StartupProbe, readinessProbe, livenessProbe
- preStop and terminationGracePeriodSeconds
- Graceful shutdown patterns in Node.js apps

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web-server
  namespace: prod
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: web-server
        image: node:18
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
        startupProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 3000
          failureThreshold: 30
          periodSeconds: 10
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 3000
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 3000
          initialDelaySeconds: 30
          periodSeconds: 15
        lifecycle:
          preStop:
            exec:
              command: ["bash","-lc","sleep 5"]
        terminationMessagePath: /dev/termination-log
        terminationMessagePolicy: File
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "100m"
            memory: "128Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "500m"
            memory: "512Mi"
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you adjust thresholds for busy traffic?
- How would you verify graceful shutdown under load?
- What pitfalls exist with preStop sleeps in container runtimes?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of InitContainer lifecycle, idempotent seeding patterns, and persistent cache management across pod restarts.

- ConfigMap-based seed script injection

## Code Example
```yaml
# Seed script ConfigMap
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: seed-scripts
data:
  seed.sh: |
    #!/bin/sh
    set -e
    if [ ! -f /cache/.seeded ]; then
      # Execute seeding logic here
      touch /cache/.seeded
    fi
---
# Deployment with InitContainer
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api-server
  namespace: ckad
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: seed-cache
        image: busybox:1.35
        command: ['/bin/sh', '/scripts/seed.sh']
        volumeMounts:
        - name: seed-scripts
          mountPath: /scripts
        - name: cache-volume
          mountPath: /cache
      containers:
      - name: api-server
        image: api-server:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: cache-volume
          mountPath: /cache
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20
      volumes:
      - name: seed-scripts
        configMap:
          name: seed-scripts
      - name: cache-volume
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: cache-pvc
```

1. **Load Testing**: Use kubectl exec to simulate concurrent requests, monitor cache seeding behavior, and verify marker file prevents re-seeding

3. **Monitoring**: Check InitContainer logs, verify probe status, and confirm cache persistence across pod restarts

## Why This Is Asked

Tests practical rollout skills: blue/green pattern, traffic routing, probes, and quick rollback under load.

- Blue/Green deployment
- Canary routing with minimal impact
- Resource requests/limits, readinessProbe, livenessProbe
- Service selector switching for traffic control

## Code Example

```yaml
# Deployment patch for canary
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web-app-canary
  namespace: prod
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: myorg/web-app:canary
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "100m"
            memory: "128Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "300m"
            memory: "256Mi"
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 5
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20
```

```yaml
# Service patched for blue/green traffic routing
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: web-app
  namespace: prod
spec:
  selector:
    app: web-app-blue
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 8080
```

```yaml
# Canary Service (optional, if using separate service for canary routing)

kind: Service
metadata:
  name: web-app-canary-svc
  namespace: prod
spec:
  selector:
    app: web-app-canary
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 8080
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests StatefulSet data isolation, config-driven rollouts, and network posture in CKAD practice.

## Key Concepts
- StatefulSet with volumeClaimTemplates
- Headless Service
- InitContainer for config
- PodTemplate annotations for rolling updates
- Resource limits and probes
- PodDisruptionBudget
- NetworkPolicy egress controls

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: collector
  namespace: sensors
spec:
  serviceName: collector-svc
  replicas: 3
  template:
    metadata:
      annotations:
        checksum/config: "abcdef"
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: config-warmup
        image: busybox
        command: ["sh","-c","cp /config/* /etc/collector/"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: config
          mountPath: /config
      containers:
      - name: collector
        image: myregistry/collector:1.2
        resources:
          requests: {cpu: "100m", memory: "128Mi"}
          limits: {cpu: "500m", memory: "256Mi"}
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet: {path: /readyz, port: 8080}
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet: {path: /livez, port: 8080}
  volumeClaimTemplates:
  - metadata:
      name: data
    spec:
      accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
      resources:
        requests:
          storage: 1Gi
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test canary upgrade vs stable in this pattern?
- How would you handle data migration if a pod resizes its PVC?
